Fixed in a87d742: CARRY_GIVE_UP_TIME is 25 seconds, after which the nest becomes the ground under his feet. Not reproduced on the test-bed, so the log line it writes is how the next report is confirmed. Six waves of Coal Town with it in, five cleared, no crash.
Fixed in a87d742: the refusal is remembered for the trip and the next interval picks the next line down. Upgrade steps a wave unchanged at a median of 17.

Measured: no engineer ever holds two built dispensers. Over four waves with a world scan counting buildings against m_hBuilder, two engineers appeared to hold two each until entities being placed or carried were excluded; then none, over four more waves. What a person sees is the blueprint in his hands while his own dispenser stands at the nest. A ghost line is written for each blueprint or carried building if anybody reports two standing.

Explained and fixed by the break freeze: a rifle sniper is one of the classes ShouldTakeUpPosition refuses, so the stale shopping flag left him with no behaviour for the whole break. Forced into a Decoy lineup afterwards he works: SniperLurk under his stack, 1970 damage and 14 kills over three waves. A fallback that made him fight without a hint was measured and thrown away, 4521 damage lurking against 570 attacking.

The Gas Passer half was already fixed by IsThrowableReady. The residual intermittent watchdog is the path budget, mvm 8fd422e: a symbolised core put the killed frame in CNavArea::GetZ under NavAreaBuildPath with maxPathLength=0, reached from the per-frame path refresh inside PlayerRunCmd, and PATHS_PER_FRAME caps the whole team at two path computations a frame. Since it landed: 41 runs and 231 waves finished with no crash at all. The rates it is measured against are 2 crashes in 9 runs on tf2ap.10 and 4 in 6 on this branch with a Gas Passer. Reopen if one appears; a core is worth taking, see docs/how-bots-break.md.

Fixed in v2.11.0. g_bShoppedThisBreak was cleared on mvm_wave_begin, which ends a break rather than starts one, so every bot that survived a wave carried 'has shopped' through the next break and GetDesiredBotAction had nothing left to offer an engineer or a medic between rounds. A bot that died shopped normally because a spawn clears the same flag, which is why it looked intermittent and why a vote restart froze the whole team. Cleared when the break opens now, on both mvm_wave_complete and mvm_wave_failed. Measured on Decoy, AUTO_BOTS, two waves cleared either way: share of between-wave samples with no behaviour, engineers 86% and 100% before, 0% and 0% after; medic 100% to 76%, and the medic's own share closed separately. The between-waves table in the run report is the instrument.

Turned from a warning into a check: run.sh reads MemAvailable and refuses to start below 1500 MB, TESTBED_MIN_FREE_MB=0 to override. The reason is in docs/testbed-metrics.md. Verified by forcing the threshold high and watching it stop. Today's 41 runs and 231 waves ran with about 4 GB available and no crash, which is the other half of the same claim.

Fixed. Not a blueprint and not a lost owner: TF2 takes a building out of the player's object list the moment he picks it up, so GetObjectOfType answered none while the engineer was carrying one. The dispenser gate then said 'no dispenser, build one', he placed a fresh one, and when the carried one went down there were two with one engineer. HasObjectOfType counts the carried one and both gates ask it. A kicked bot was ruled out by test: kicking an engineer holding a level three dispenser removed it and left no orphan. Six waves of Coal Town with relocation on: five cleared, no crash, never more than one dispenser at once, sentry uptime 72 per cent.

Implemented and measured. The button is pressed now: MedicProjectileShield puts the shield up when the rage meter is full and something is shooting near his patient, and generate rage on heal is no longer refused in IsUpgradeWasted when the feature is on. It fires 26 to 35 times a run, logged, so a null result cannot be mistaken for a behaviour that never ran.

Three arms against the 24 attempt baseline on Bavarian Botbash wave 1: held 176s/58 robots, 240s/83, and 175s/60, against a baseline of 160s and 58 with quartiles of 154-192 and 52-64. The middle arm is outside the band on both and did not replicate, and the first shared the machine with another server. Two of three sit inside the band.

So it ships off, behind medic_shield, and the item's own premise is settled: the wiki is right that a person should press it, and this mod can now press it. Whether it is worth three hundred credits is what the switch is for.

Fixed and measured. A Rescue Ranger bolt repairs a building and does not reload one; only a wrench hit puts shells back. A sentry at full health with an empty magazine still answers yes to SentryNeedsMetal, so CanRepairFromRange let the engineer stand across the map firing bolts into something already whole, forever. From his point of view he was fixing it, which is why it reads as refusing.

Range repair is for damage only now. The building samples carry the magazine, which nothing counted before.

Coal Town, six waves each way with the Rescue Ranger loadout: samples of a full health sentry under fifty shells 21 of 126 before and 6 of 116 after, median magazine 104 to a full 200, five of six waves cleared either way. Not map specific as far as this shows: the mechanism is the weapon, not Decoy.

Measured rather than assumed, and it is mostly already what he asks for. Across every run in results/, 1441 stretches of an engineer alive inside a wave with no dispenser of his own: median 20 seconds, quartiles 10 to 25, which is the time it takes him to walk over and build one. So he does prioritise it.

The tail is real though: 58 stretches over a minute and a worst of 165 seconds. The cause is in the code rather than in the measurement - the dispenser branch in CTFBotMvMEngineerIdle_Update only fires when m_ctSentrySafe is in the future, so on a wave where the sentry is under fire continuously he never gets a window and the dispenser stays down for the rest of it. That is a defensible order, the sentry is the nest, and it is also exactly the wave where the team would want the dispenser.

Closing as measured. If it should change, the change is that gate and the number to hold it against is the tail above, not the median.

Fixed and measured, and both halves of the report were the same cause.

The sighting rule in Event_PlayerDeath was 'a Spy killed somebody on another team', which a defending Spy satisfies every time he stabs a robot. So the player's own Spy put his whole team on alert, which is why this only happens when somebody plays Spy. A sighting is now a robot's Spy.

The suspect finder also skipped no humans, so a player could be picked as the disguised one. Every robot in this mode is a fake client, so a real player on RED cannot be an enemy Spy. The price is a human on BLU via the mod's join-blue command being unstabbable, which is smaller than a Spy player being frisked by his own team.

Measured with a friendly Spy in the lineup: 187 of 3443 samples spy checking before, 0 of 1676 after. Two lineups without a Spy spent 0 of 8273 samples spy checking, so the trigger was never an actual robot Spy. Firing with a teammate in the crosshair is unchanged at 15 to 18 per cent, which is bots shooting past one another rather than at them, and harmless with friendly fire off.

Fixed in e20deb3. The six SniperSpot origins are restored from 5aedaff and the TEMPORARILY REMOVED comment is gone. Config_LoadMap should read 6 sniper on Decoy again. Swept every other map config: no other leftover test marker. Community maps have no nests, dispensers or teleporters at all, which is incomplete surveying rather than a leftover, and is not this bead.

Fixed in e20deb3. The exit now tries a ring at BUSTER_BLAST_RANGE + 100 all the way round before falling back to the old 150-unit ring, so a cramped map still gets an exit rather than none. Root cause was narrower than the bead said: Decoy names one TeleporterExit spot and NearestFreeExitSpot hands it to the first engineer, so with two engineers the second finds it taken, returns false, and drops to the nest-anchored fallback. That fallback was the unsafe path.
Fixed. UpdateDefenderReadiness moved above the upgrade-zone early return in CTFBotTacticalMonitor_Update, which is what its own comment already claimed. Compiles clean, warning count unchanged at 54.
Fixed. ReadyDefender ends TFCond_Taunting before setting ready, only on the readying path. Not reproduced against a looping taunt, which is the case that turns a delay into a hang; noted in the bead.

Measured and acted on. Six waves of Decoy per arm, same build, only sm_redbots_feature_engineer_disposable moved. Defender deaths per wave: off [0,3,5,7,9,10] against on [11,12,14,15,15,17], so the spreads do not touch and the worst wave without the mini beat the best wave with it. Sentries lost 7 against 14, robots killed 73 against 36.5 median, waves cleared 3 of 6 against 2 of 6. The switch now ships off, which is what EZKSupernova asked for. Caveats: one map, six waves an arm, and the arms ran under different machine load; deaths are far less load-sensitive than durations and the separation is total, but a second map is worth running. The rest of his ask, PDA before weapons and resistances, is untouched and belongs in its own bead if it is still wanted.

Fixed and verified on the testbed. Cause was a one-frame race in engineerbuilddispenser.sp: VS_PressFireButton puts the building down on the next tick, and GetObjectOfType was asked in the same frame, so the answer was always none, the action continued, the toolbox re-armed and it pressed again. The check now runs before the press and ends the action as soon as a dispenser exists, and a press gets a tick to land before another is allowed. Four waves of Decoy: 18 duplicate events before, 0 after, with 138 dispensers and 138 sentries still sampled so the engineers build normally. listed:2 in the before-run ruled out the other candidate: the game's object list saw both, so no gate was blind and the fix did not belong in GetObjectOfType. engineerbuildsentrygun.sp has the same shape and got the same guard, recognised rather than measured. Still unexplained: TF2 normally allows one dispenser per engineer, and why the game permitted a second is unknown; the fix stops the press rather than relying on the game to refuse.

Filed on a wrong inference. I thought the crash count included install-time restarts because each 'core dumped' was preceded by 'installed the bots and the statistics plugin'; that line prints every thirty seconds for the whole run, so it separates nothing. run.sh already scopes the count to this run's window and was right. What it could still do is print the cause, and that is worth having: 'crashed 1 time(s)' and 'the watchdog killed it after an engineer was stuck 12s' send you to different places. Refiled as that, narrowly.
Done. run.sh now says which kind of crash it was and prints the two commands that turn the newest core into a stack. Verified against tonight's logs.

Not a CBaseNPC bug. The testbed was copying a live mapped .so over itself because build.sh gave the staged prebuilt extensions a new mtime on every build. Fixed with cp -p, verified stable across rebuilds.

Built, in both interfaces, with docs. The catalogue is generated from the mod's pools and the game's schema, the resolution layer is botloadout.Library with the custom: key, and the Loadouts page builds and names them. No mod change was needed: GetServerLoadoutWeapon takes whatever index the file carries.

Built and shipped in v2.18.1: the lineup changes on a running mission from the Bot Switcher tab in both interfaces, from the settings save, and from !ap bots. Money survives it, measured on a live server. Documented in both languages. What is left is a play-test with a human on RED, filed separately, because that is confirmation rather than work.
